title: Vintage Gibson L-0 & L-00: Value and Authentication Guide
description: Compare the early all-mahogany L-0, revived black L-0 and sunburst L-00, with identification photos, factory-number clues and 2026 guide-based values.
h1: Gibson L-0 & L-00 Value and Authentication Guide
alt: 1930s Gibson L-00 in sunburst with a firestripe pickguard and rectangular bridge
caption: The sunburst L-00 from my 1930s Reverb listing, shown alongside an early all-mahogany L-0 and a later black L-0 below.

faqs.q: Are the Gibson L-0 and L-00 the same model?
faqs.a: They are closely related, and later examples can be nearly identical. The L-0 name also covers an earlier design and was reused in 1937. Identify the period, body, top wood and trim before choosing a model name or value row.

faqs.q: Does black finish always mean L-0?
faqs.a: No. Black is strongly associated with the revived 1937 to 1942 L-0, but black L-00s also exist. Finish, binding, body dimensions, neck joint and dating evidence must be considered together.

faqs.q: Where should I look for a factory order number?
faqs.a: Photograph the neck block inside the body and the back of the headstock. Some late-1930s examples carry stamped numbers on the headstock. Preserve the location, letters and spacing; an unreadable mark should not be turned into an exact year.

faqs.q: What do the value ranges represent?
faqs.a: They are 2026 price-guide references reduced by fixed percentages of 11% to 15%, with both endpoints adjusted together. They assume an excellent original instrument and are not recorded sale prices, a guaranteed purchase offer or an insurance appraisal.
